title: Fallen Nights now has a browser demo. Does the scrap-or-escape decision make sense?
author: WalkingDadPG
selftext:
I shared an art-style comparison here a couple of weeks ago. Some of you pointed out that the water competed with the terrain and the UI was hard to read. That was useful feedback: nicer individual AI assets don’t automatically make a clearer game.



Fallen Nights is a small top-down survival game. You collect scrap, build defenses and repair a boat to escape. Defenses and boat repairs use the same scrap, so spending more to survive tonight delays getting out.



I’m building it with AI-generated code and art, first with Claude Code and now Codex. The useful loop has been asking for a small change, playing it, then describing exactly what felt wrong. “Make it better” gives me much less to work with than “I couldn’t tell why the boat repair stopped.”



The browser demo is now at [https://fallennights.com](https://fallennights.com)



If you try it: what was the first moment you weren’t sure what to do? I’m particularly interested in whether that scrap trade-off becomes clear without me explaining it.



I also recorded the process, including earlier versions: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3voLQnBpbE](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=t3voLQnBpbE)
